Police officers and rangers have stepped up joint patrols in Poland’s mountainous Tatra National Park during the peak summer season, following a spate of rule-breaking including swimming in the park’s lakes and ponds, driving cars and going off marked trails. Meanwhile, national park authorities have repeated warnings that bathing, littering and breaking other rules can damage the park’s fragile ecosystem. Local police officers have joined Tatra National Park rangers on patrols on popular tourist routes. On one such patrol last week, officers focused on education and prevention, reminding visitors not to leave marked trails or litter and explaining how to behave safely and responsibly in the mountains. They also checked that organised groups were accompanied by qualified mountain guides, as required by law. Fines for such offences range from 50 zloty (€11.55) to as much as 1,000 zloty (€231) in the event of environmental damage or multiple offences. Police said that all visitors encountered during the patrol were complying with the park’s regulations. However, they added that similar patrols would continue on a regular basis. The Tatra National Park, home to Poland’s highest peaks, and the nearby mountain resort of Zakopane are among the country’s most popular holiday destinations, with crowds taking to park trails in the summer season. The park, the most visited of Poland’s 23 national parks, welcomed a record 5.3 million visitors in 2025 and offers 275 km of marked hiking trails, including high-altitude routes that connect at several points with the adjacent national park in Slovakia. 🚨 Ukraiński Influencer wjechał nielegalnie samochodem na Morskie oko 🗣️: Jesteśmy pierwszymi ludźmi w historii, którzy wjechali samochodem nad Morskie Oko. To było jedno z miejsc, do których chcieliśmy dotrzeć podczas tej podróży i wszyscy znajomi oraz przyjaciele mówili, że… pic.twitter.com/tA9shZ6Rqk — Pigułka 💊 (@informacyjnie) May 23, 2026 This season has already seen a number of high-profile cases of transgressions of the park’s strict rules. In May, a Ukrainian social media influencer sparked outrage after driving a sports car along a road closed to traffic to Morskie Oko, a picturesque lake nestled between the mountains. As a result, he was banned from entering Poland and other Schengen Area countries for five years. Tourists have also been filmed entering Morskie Oko and other protected lakes and ponds, which is not permitted in the national park. This month, a group of young Dutch tourists were filmed bathing in Przedni Staw Polski in the Valley of the Five Lakes, one of the Tatras’ best-known hiking destinations. Witnesses repeatedly warned the group that entering the lake was prohibited, but they ignored the warnings, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. Park authorities have responded to such incidents by reminding visitors of the reasons for the strict rules. “Tatra ponds are incredibly delicate ecosystems. Cosmetics, UV filters, insect repellents, and bacteria entering the water can have a long-lasting impact on its chemical composition and the organisms living in the lakes,” they warned. A national park in Poland’s southern mountains has completed testing of an electric bus that could replace horse-drawn carriages carrying tourists to a famous lake. World.title: Polish opposition PiS party set to split, with over 30 MPs being expelled
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. More than 30 MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, have effectively resigned after refusing to sign a loyalty pledge, party leader Jarosław Kaczyński has announced. The dispute centres around a more moderate faction in the party aligned with former prime minister and deputy PiS leader Mateusz Morawiecki, who is one of those now set to be expelled from the party. They have for months been unhappy with PiS’s move in a hard-right direction. 💬 Prezes PiS Jarosław Kaczyński @OficjalnyJK. 👉 Udostępnij pic.twitter.com/bycjE0Yq0f — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) July 24, 2026 “Around 30-something…of our group’s MPs have resigned,” revealed Kaczyński at a press conference on Friday. He added that their departures would be formalised at a meeting of the party’s political committee scheduled for Tuesday next week. Kaczyński’s announcement came after a deadline expired at midnight on Thursday for its MPs to sign a pledge of loyalty to the party that included a commitment not to be members of any external political associations. That measure was aimed in particular at an association called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) founded by Morawiecki in April. The former prime minister had always insisted that his organisation was intended as complementary to PiS, rather than a rival to it. However, many figures in the party saw it as an attempt by Morawiecki to create a separate centre of power, and potentially to use the association as a launchpad for creating his own party ahead of the autumn 2027 parliamentary elections. The right-wing opposition PiS party has threatened disciplinary action, including exclusion from electoral lists, against dozens of its MPs who have joined a new internal group led by former PM @MorawieckiM and intended to appeal to more moderate voters https://t.co/y62Cm361U2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 17, 2026 After PiS issued a resolution on Wednesday last week requiring that its parliamentarians pledge to withdraw from any such associations, most of its 186 MPs quickly complied. However, a group of between 30 and 40 who are part of Development Plus refused to do so. “Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” said Kaczyński on Friday. “And so they made the decision they did.” “In this situation, we cannot view the [Development Plus] association as anything other than a component of a plan…to split our party,” he added. However, although its supporters will now leave PiS, “we want to part ways without any animosity”, said Kaczyński. After Kaczyński’s announcement, senior figures from Development Plus made clear that no one from their association had resigned from PiS. They had simply not signed the declaration of loyalty demanded by the party. Later, Morawiecki himself held a press conference in parliament surrounded by his supporters. He claimed that an unnamed “small group of schemers” within PiS had been seeking to turn Kaczyński against him and push him out of the party. “We fought for the unity of Law and Justice until the very end,” declared Morawiecki, who said that his group included 40 MPs, one senator and three MEPs. However, three of the MPs are not members of PiS, and therefore were not expected to sign the loyalty declaration. Szanowni Państwo! 🟦Do ostatniej chwili walczyłem o jedność Prawa i Sprawiedliwości. Nie o stanowiska. Nie o osobiste ambicje. Nie o wpływy. 🟦Walczyłem o jedność obozu, który przez osiem lat zmieniał Polskę – budował jej bezpieczeństwo, rozwijał gospodarkę i przywracał godność… pic.twitter.com/PP7sOkzMHp — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 24, 2026 If the expulsion of Morawiecki’s supporters is confirmed, it will mark a major shake-up of Poland’s political landscape. PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, PiS has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemyszław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Morawiecki, who was an international banker before joining PiS to become finance minister and then prime minister, wants the party to focus on more technocratic issues, such as economic development, rather than Euroscepticism and culture wars. That has led to frequent public sparring between his supporters and others in the party. In April, PiS threatened disciplinary action against members of Development Plus. Kaczyński and Morawiecki then reached an agreement that allowed the association to continue. But that uneasy truce has now fallen apart. World.title: Polish president renews bid for referendum on EU climate policy
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has submitted a second request to parliament for a nationwide referendum on whether Poland should continue implementing the European Union’s climate policies, which he argues are too costly. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, first proposed a referendum in May. But it was rejected by the Senate, the upper house of parliament, where the more liberal government has a majority. Senators argued that the proposed referendum question was “absurd”. The president has now submitted a revised proposal featuring a simplified question and again proposed holding the referendum on 27 September this year. Nawrocki’s originally proposed question was: “Are you in favour of implementing EU climate policy, which has led to an increase in citizens’ cost of living, energy prices and the cost of running business and agricultural activity?” However, following criticism in the Senate that the question was clearly intended to elicit a specific answer, this time he has proposed a more neutral one: “Are you in favour of Poland implementing the European Union’s climate policy?” “I’m looking for compromises, looking for solutions,” said Nawrocki on Thursday while announcing the new referendum bid. “The Senate wasn’t satisfied with the [previous] question”, so “we prepared a different one…[that] does not suggest anything”. However, the president has also proposed that the ballot paper would include information on what answering “yes” or “no” would mean in practice. Voters would be told, for example, that maintaining EU climate policy would result in, among other things, “Poland bearing costs estimated at 3.5 trillion zloty by 2040”, “burdens on agriculture”, “increasing costs for industry” and “obligations for owners of buildings”. By contrast, voting “no” would mean “negotiating exceptions and exemptions for Poland with the relevant EU bodies that will protect Polish industry and citizens from the burdens of climate policy”. Poland's right-wing opposition wants to withdraw from the EU Emissions Trading System, saying it makes Poles "a cash machine for absurd leftist climate policies"@PStrzalkowski explains what costs ETS really brings, and what prospects there are for reform https://t.co/UxpMWpG1pE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 4, 2026 Under Poland’s constitution, the president may call a referendum with the approval of a majority of senators in a vote where at least half of all members of the 100-seat chamber are present. The ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk controls 63 seats in the Senate, making approval of proposals brought forward by Nawrocki, who often clashes with the government and regularly vetoes its bills, unlikely. While the government is generally pro-EU, it has also been critical of Brussels’ green policies, arguing that they place too great a burden on Poland. After the European Commission last Friday unveiled changes intended to soften the impact of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS), the EU’s flagship climate policy, they were welcomed by the Polish government as a step in the right direction. Dzisiaj robimy milowy krok w zmianie systemu ETS. Po raz pierwszy Komisja Europejska proponuje rozwiązania, które łagodzą, a nie zaostrzają wpływ systemu na gospodarkę i obywateli. To efekt konsekwentnych działań Polski i zbudowania silnej koalicji państw w UE. Dzisiejsza… pic.twitter.com/5AMd9KCBVa — Ministerstwo Klimatu i Środowiska (@MKiS_GOV_PL) July 17, 2026 However, in his written justification for the new referendum proposal, Nawrocki wrote that, while he had “given the government time” in its push for ETS reform, the final result was simply “technical adjustments” that postpone some elements but do “not change the direction” or ultimate outcome. “ETS will remain an increasingly expensive, increasingly extensive system, and increasingly burdensome for the Polish economy,” wrote the president. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which is the main opposition and supported Nawrocki’s bid for the presidency last year, wants Poland to unilaterally withdraw from ETS. Government figures warn, however, that there is no way to do so without either accruing enormous fines or leaving the EU entirely. When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Nawrocki’s new referendum proposal was met with criticism by figures from the ruling coalition. “There is no possibility of one country suspending part of EU law,” wrote Stanisław Gawłowski, a senator from Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO) party. “This referendum is pure fraud.” Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, also from KO, wrote that, “as the Brits have learned, the Europhobe’s dream world, in which one enjoys all the privileges of EU membership without any obligations, does not exist”. However, Nawrocki’s initiative was welcomed by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of PiS, who wrote that, “on such fundamental matters as climate policy, Poles should decide, not Brussels bureaucrats”. Zaproponowane przez @NawrockiKn pytanie referendalne jest wybiórcze. Kontrpropozycja: „Czy jesteś za likwidacją unijnych dopłat do inwestycji i dla rolników?” Jak przekonali się Brytyjczycy, świat eurofoba, w którym ma się same przywileje członkostwa w UE, nie istnieje. — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) July 23, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland appoints new human rights commissioner
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government’s majority in parliament has chosen Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram as Poland’s new human rights commissioner. She will take office after the five-year term of the incumbent, Marcin Wiącek, expires today. Gregorczyk-Abram is a prominent lawyer and activist, who is particularly well known for opposing the overhaul of the judiciary by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. PiS, which is now the main opposition party, strongly opposed her election, arguing that she is politically aligned with the current, more liberal government. Gregorczyk-Abram herself, however, has pledged to “put all my beliefs and views aside” when she takes up the new role. Senat wyraził zgodę na powołanie Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram na Rzecznika Praw Obywatelskich. pic.twitter.com/gz3rwGy3hi — Senat RP 🇵🇱 (@PolskiSenat) July 22, 2026 The commissioner for human rights (widely known by its Polish initials, RPO) is appointed by a resolution of the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, with the consent of the upper-house Senate. Candidates must meet certain requirements, including not belonging to any political party and having legal expertise and relevant experience. As well as acting as a watchdog for human rights, the RPO also has the power to submit motions to the Constitutional Tribunal to assess the constitutionality of laws and to file so-called cassation appeals to the Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court against rulings by lower courts. Poland’s human rights commissioner has written to the government expressing concern that a "temporary" ban on asylum claims by most migrants who irregularly cross the border from Belarus remains in place after more than a year https://t.co/9SA2TypQdK — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 28, 2026 Gregorczyk-Abram was last month nominated as a candidate to be the new RPO by the main ruling party, Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), along with one of its coalition partners, The Left (Lewica). PiS proposed a rival candidate, Adam Borowski, a veteran of Poland’s anti-communist struggle in the 1980s. However, critics argued that Borowski, an activist and former PiS election candidate, does not appear to have the requisite legal knowledge and experience. In a Sejm vote last Friday, the ruling coalition supported Gregorczyk-Abram, who won 233 votes to Borowski’s 177. On Wednesday, her candidacy was also supported by the Senate, with 59 votes in favour and 25 against, confirming that she will become the new RPO. Gregorczyk-Abram is best known as one of the founders and leaders of the Free Courts (Wolne Sądy) initiative launched in 2017 amid a wave of protests against the then-PiS government’s efforts to take greater control over the judiciary. Free Courts was prominent in efforts to defend the rule of law. Many of its leading figures are now associated with the current ruling coalition: Maria Ejchart is a deputy justice minister, while Michał Wawrykiewicz is a member of the European Parliament representing KO. In April last year, Gregorczyk-Abram was made chairwoman of a commission established by the current government to look into cases of abuse of power against civil society under the former PiS administration. In September, her commission published its first findings, in which it said that public media outlets under PiS control had “carried out systematic repressive and defamatory actions against activists, non-governmental organisations, and civil society”. Poland's public media “carried out systematic repressive actions against activists, NGOs and civil society” during the rule of the former PiS government, a report commissioned by the new government has found https://t.co/S2MO9KGssC — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 26, 2025 PiS argues that Gregorczyk-Abram’s previous activity makes her unsuitable as a suitable candidate for RPO, which is meant to be a non-partisan role. They also point to claims that she was involved in a group of legal figures that discussed the Tusk government’s controversial takeover of public media in December 2023. “[She] is a discredited and extremely politicised person who should be brought to justice, and not receive the laurels of the commissioner for human rights,” former PiS justice minister Marcin Warchoł told the Do Rzeczy weekly last month. After a Sejm committee hearing on Gregorczyk-Abram’s candidacy earlier this month, former PiS deputy justice minister Sebastian Kaleta criticised her for ignoring questions over her alleged “role in the illegal takeover of public media”. Zadałem Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram serię pytań o jej działania i możliwe spotkania z Ewą Wrzosek w sprawie przejęcia TVP, w tym możliwego tworzenia dokumentów prokuratorskich w prywatnej kancelarii. Kandydatka ostentacyjnie zdecydowała się ignorować te pytania. Ma bardzo dużo do… — Sebastian Kaleta (@sjkaleta) July 15, 2026 Speaking to state broadcaster TVP on Wednesday after her appointment was confirmed by the Senate, Gregorczyk-Abram declared that, “from the moment I take the oath and assume the position of commissioner, I will be independent and sovereign”. She pledged to “put all my beliefs and views – because each of us has them – aside and become an advocate for all citizens, regardless of what they believe in, how they live, or who they vote for”. Gregorczyk-Abram said that among her priorities as RPO would be the justice system, supporting the rights of disabled people and their carers, protecting older people, and fighting hate speech. With regard to the last of these issues, she noted that certain politicians present some groups as “enemies”, pointing to how this previously happened with LGBT+ people and judges, and is now being directed towards Ukrainians. Those are all groups who have at various stages been targeted by PiS and other right-wing parties. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: President to swear in new judge to Poland’s disputed constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has agreed to swear in a new judge to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), ending weeks of doubt as to whether the opposition-aligned president would accept the judge appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority. Although Sławomir Patyra will now be accepted onto the court, four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year continue to be excluded after Nawrocki refused to receive their oaths and the TK’s chief justice, also aligned with the opposition, blocked them from taking office. W najbliższy wtorek 28 lipca Prezydent Karol Nawrocki działając na postawie art. 4 ust. 1 ustawy o statusie sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, przyjmie ślubowanie od prof. Sławomira Patyry i tego samego dnia wręczy powołania czterem nowym sędziom Sądu Najwyższego. W przyszłym… — Zbigniew Bogucki🇵🇱 (@BoguckiZbigniew) July 22, 2026 Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK – for example when a judge’s nine-year term expires – the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again this week, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. Patyra himself has also made clear on which side of the dispute he stands. In an interview with news website Onet in May, he accused Nawrocki and Święczkowski of “blatantly unlawful actions” in deciding which TK judges can and cannot take office and suggested that the police should intervene. Sędzia TK prof. Patyra po raz kolejny zaapelował do Prezydenta o wyznaczenie mu terminu na złożenie przysięgi. Ignorowanie sędziego TK przez Prezydenta jest kolejnym przykładem psucia państwa. To pokazuje, jak bardzo siły anty-demokratyczne boją się odbudowy niezależnego TK.… — Dariusz Mazur (@_Dariusz_Mazur) July 21, 2026 Finally, on Wednesday this week, Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, announced that Nawrocki had invited Patyra to the presidential palace on Tuesday next week to take his oath. Speaking to Polsat News, Bogucki said that, in the case of Patyra, initially “there were some doubts, but the president dispelled them”, without specifying what they were. In the end, they concluded that “we had a fundamentally clean situation here” and Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”, unlike the six new judges chosen by the Sejm in March to fill longstanding vacancies. “It was not President Nawrocki or the current opposition who destroyed and are destroying the tribunal; it is the government that is doing it,” he added. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. World.title: Germany deploys soldiers to Poland to help reinforce eastern borders
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany has deployed soldiers to Poland to help reinforce defences on NATO’s eastern flank in response to the threat of Russia. While Poland already hosts various allied forces, the presence of German troops is particularly symbolic given the two countries’ difficult history. “United, we will prevail,” wrote the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces (SGWP), announcing the deployment. “This is what allied cooperation looks like in practice, which translates into greater military readiness and strengthens NATO’s defensive potential.” Polscy i niemieccy żołnierze razem wzmacniają granicę z Rosją. Takie rzeczy możliwe tylko za Tuska ☺️ pic.twitter.com/oNBME2gBsv — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 22, 2026 Last December, the Polish and German defence ministries revealed that a “mid-double-digit number” of German troops would be deployed from mid-2026 until the end of 2027 to support implementation of Poland’s East Shield operation, which seeks to bolster defences along the borders with Belarus and Russia. They said that the German personnel would mainly engage in engineering work, such as digging trenches, laying barbed wire and constructing anti-tank barriers. Today, Poland’s SGWP confirmed that “several dozen” German troops, including “highly specialised engineering forces” along with their equipment, had since June been temporarily deployed to “support the Polish armed forces in expanding defence infrastructure on NATO’s northeastern flank”. It emphasised that the East Shield project is “purely defensive in nature” and comes in “response to threats stemming from, among others, Russian aggression against Ukraine”. While the armed forces did not reveal the location of the deployment, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk indicated in a social media post that it was on the Russian border. Poland has a 210-km frontier with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. German public broadcaster Deutsche Welle reports that the activities of the German sappers are focused in particular on improving defences around the so-called Suwałki Gap, a strategically important stretch of land around the Polish-Lithuanian border between Belarus and Kaliningrad. “Together, we are ensuring Europe’s security,” said Lieutenant General Alexander Sollfrank, the Bundeswehr’s operational commander, announcing the deployment today. “Through our engagement in Poland, we are strengthening NATO’s defence capabilities and underscoring the alliance’s unwavering commitment to ensuring peace through unity and credible deterrence.” Poland and Germany have signed a bilateral security agreement that will see the two neighbours and NATO allies increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity https://t.co/6BPX2WxvxH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 17, 2026 SGWP, which shared footage of Polish and German forces installing anti-tank barriers, said the work aims to “hinder and delay an aggressor’s actions in the event of a threat”, thereby “increasing the time for a response from the Polish armed forces and the entire [NATO] alliance”. It also seeks to “create conditions for the efficient reception, deployment and use of NATO forces on Polish territory”. SGWP welcomed “the involvement of the German contingent as a practical expression of allied solidarity and the result of consistently developing military cooperation between Poland and Germany”. It also noted that the cooperation would help the two sides improve their ability to operate jointly, including “developing the competencies necessary for conducting a joint defence operation”. However, it emphasised that the current deployment is focused on training and engineering, with no combat component, and that the German troops are unarmed. SGWP also emphasised that the East Shield operation remains entirely a Polish national programme. The leaders of eight countries on the EU's eastern flank have met in the first summit of its kind to discuss closer security cooperation. Finland and Poland announced that they would jointly lead an initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, to bolster defences https://t.co/fxRHpkM6w9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 The deployment of German troops to Poland comes shortly after the two countries signed a defence cooperation agreement in which they pledged to increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity. The agreement is a sign that the two countries now stand “shoulder to shoulder, as equals”, declared German defence minister Boris Pistorius. Poland is also currently seeking a new permanent US military base on its territory, after President Donald Trump recently pledged to boost American troop numbers. Last week, Tusk also announced that Poland will host military exercises involving France and the UK this autumn. Poland will host military exercises later this year with France and the UK to prepare for providing future security guarantees to Ukraine, says PM @donaldtusk. He also declared Poland's willingness to permanently host more troops from its European allies https://t.co/couian4FrP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 14, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Poland’s climate and environment ministry has inaugurated the first of 11 planned “community forests” around large cities, with the aim of giving residents a place for recreation and contact with nature while also helping to fulfil the government’s pledge to reduce logging. Plans for the forests were announced in 2024, and the first has now been established around Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city. Ten other major urban centres, including Warsaw, Kraków, Poznań and Łódź, are set to follow. Dotrzymujemy słowa. Powołaliśmy pierwsze lasy społeczne w Polsce, to lasy ochronne wokół Wrocławia. Kolejne miasta przed nami. @MKiS_GOV_PL pic.twitter.com/RxhsMZShj9 — Paulina Hennig-Kloska (@hennigkloska) July 21, 2026 “This is a historic moment and the beginning of a new approach to forest protection – with residents in mind first and foremost,” said climate and environment minister Paulina Hennig-Kloska at an inauguration ceremony outside Wrocław on Sunday. “Community forests are places where residents can relax, play sports and simply spend time close to nature,” she added. “At the same time, they are crucial to our security and quality of life: they retain water, regulate the climate, purify the air and protect the soil.” An area covering 13,000 hectares (32,124 acres) has been designated as a community forest around Wrocław. Forest management there will now be aimed at “maximising the forest’s social functions”, says the ministry, while timber harvesting is also restricted. The area will be divided into three zones, including “natural forests”, where nature will be left to take its course, and “near-natural forests” with minimal intervention. However, the largest zone, amounting to over 8,000 hectares, will be “social forests”, which the state forestry agency says “will be managed in a way that ensures the comfort of those who use the forest and its benefits related to wellbeing, physical exercise and recreation”. Hennig-Kloska noted that, in the latter area, educational trails as well as hiking and cycling paths would be established. However, given that such facilities already exist in many forests, it remains unclear how the new community forests will differ. The ministry is now conducting consultations and analysis on establishing community forests around ten other designated urban centres: Bielsko-Biała, Tricity (Gdańsk-Gdynia-Sopot), Katowice, Kielce, Kraków, Łódź, Poznań, Szczecin, Toruń-Bydgoszcz and Warsaw. On Sunday, Hennig-Kloska said that the “next in line” to have their community forests established are Kielce and Bielsko-Biała, reported the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Shortly after coming to power in December 2023, the current government announced that it would halt planned logging in some forests. The former Law and Justice (PiS) administration had faced criticism for overseeing an increase in logging, especially in Białowieża Forest. The current government also launched plans to create Poland’s first new national parks in over two decades. However, PiS-aligned President Karol Nawrocki last year vetoed that move, arguing that it would “block the economic development of the region” and threaten Poland’s security. World.title: Hungaroring F1 highlights: Ferrari dominate opening day as Antonelli struggles
World.content:
Ferrari made an emphatic start to the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix weekend, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton topping the two Friday practice sessions at the Hungaroring. While the Italian team controlled the opening-day Hungaroring F1 highlights, championship leader Kimi Antonelli struggled for pace and confidence in his Mercedes.

Ferrari set the standard at the Hungaroring

Leclerc led the opening practice session with a lap of 1:19.075, finishing 0.484 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen. Hamilton took third place in the second Ferrari, giving the team an encouraging start at the circuit in Mogyoród, just outside Budapest.

The session did not end entirely smoothly for Leclerc. A mechanical problem forced him to stop near the pit-lane entrance during the final ten minutes, leaving Ferrari with additional checks to complete before FP2. Lance Stroll also suffered a rear-suspension failure, spinning his upgraded Aston Martin and causing a red flag.

Ferrari’s advantage became even clearer in the afternoon. Hamilton set the fastest lap of the day with a 1:18.729, beating Leclerc by 0.148 seconds and completing a Ferrari one-two. Lando Norris finished third for McLaren, followed by Verstappen and George Russell.

Formula 1’s official FP1 highlights and FP2 highlights show the main moments from Friday’s running.

Antonelli’s difficult first day in Hungary

Antonelli missed FP1 as Mercedes gave reserve driver Frederik Vesti an opportunity behind the wheel. Vesti finished seventh, while Russell placed fifth.

The championship leader returned for FP2 but encountered serious balance and braking problems. Antonelli reported that he had nearly spun twice under braking and repeatedly locked the rear wheels. He eventually finished only 13th, 1.964 seconds behind Hamilton and more than a second slower than Mercedes teammate Russell.

The second practice session was interrupted when Franco Colapinto lost control of his Alpine at the final corner and crashed backwards into the barrier. Stroll did not participate as Aston Martin continued repairing the damage caused by his FP1 suspension failure.

World.title: Large-scale, unexplained brown pollution contaminates Hungarian river — authorities respond, video, updated
World.content:
Efforts to remove a pollution discovered on Thursday in the River Fekete-Körös are set to begin on Friday afternoon, according to a statement issued by the Körös Regional Water Directorate (Kövizig) to the Hungarian news agency MTI. Preliminary results from official water samples are also expected to arrive later on Friday.

Preparations for on-site intervention are already under way, the authority said. Necessary fieldwork is being carried out to clear accumulated debris, ensuring that heavy machinery and transport vehicles can safely access the affected area.

The substantial mass of debris — believed, according to press reports, to be cattle manure — is currently stable. A submerged barrier installed to prevent its spread continues to contain the pollution, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

Water abstraction points within the Békés weir system remain temporarily closed, the statement added. Two designated bathing areas on the Körös rivers, at Szanazug and Városerdő, have been shut. Further measures will depend on laboratory analysis of water samples taken at multiple locations.

Water quality damage control operations continue under a third-degree alert level, the authority confirmed.

Later, the authorities said they had removed the pollution from the affected stretch of the river.

World.title: Other public institution, state-owned company heads dismissed by Magyar government – names revealed
World.content:
The Ministry of Social Relations and Culture has terminated the employment of the directors of the Natural History Museum, the National Széchényi Library and the Museum of Applied Arts, following a comprehensive institutional review of cultural background institutions, aimed at ensuring workplace safety, predictability and professional integrity. Furthermore, Minister István Kapitány fired the CEO of Paks II.

Three national collection heads sent away

The dismissal of Zsolt Bernert, Dávid Róza and Zoltán Cselovszki, respectively, came after a review which included consultations with institution leaders, works councils, representative bodies and dozens of employees, the ministry said in a statement quoted by the Hungarian news agency.

Minister Zoltán Tarr also ordered a comprehensive professional, economic and ethical internal investigation at the Hungarian National Museum’s Public Collection Centre (MNM KK), a supervising body of the museums.

The ministry has begun preparations to decentralise the MNM KK, enabling its affiliated institutions to operate with strengthened professional autonomy. The process will involve institution leaders, representative bodies and employees, with the goal of establishing a collection system that ensures a safe work environment, professional autonomy and long-term sustainable operations, the statement said.

Paks II CEO also sacked

Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said he had dismissed Gergely Jákli, the CEO of Paks II Nuclear Power Plant, in a post on Facebook on Friday. Kapitány said he would introduce the new CEO of the power plant expansion in the afternoon.

World.title: Shocking video: police search for men travelling on the side of a train in Hungary
World.content:
Unknown individuals chose to travel on the side of a train in Érd, according to footage shared by the local police.

Uknown men travelled on the side of a train

According to a video uploaded to the official YouTube page of the Hungarian police, unidentified men travelled on the side of a passenger train departing from Érd. In the late afternoon of 1 June, they jumped onto the side of a moving train at Érd railway station. They remained there until the next stop, Érd-felső, before jumping off and fleeing the scene.

One of the perpetrators. Photo: PrtScr/Youtube

The local police are asking anyone who recognises the individuals, who were risking their lives, to contact the Pest County Police Headquarters on +36 1 236 2897, or to submit an anonymous report via the Telefontanú (Phone Witness) service on +36 80 555 111, or by calling the central emergency number 112.

They added that travelling on the side of a train can easily lead to life-threatening situations, particularly when the carriages contract. Furthermore, individuals can easily fall while the train is travelling at high speed, or be struck by high-voltage overhead wires.

Check out the video below:

Teenagers died after climbing on a freight train

In a separate incident, a 17-year-old boy and a 16-year-old girl climbed onto a freight train in Budapest and came dangerously close to a 25 kV overhead wire. Although they did not touch it, both were fatally struck by an electric arc. Such phenomena can cause death even from several metres away. This is one of the reasons why entering areas near high-voltage equipment is strictly prohibited, vaol.hu wrote.

If you missed: Epstein scandal reaches Hungary again after unexpected death of agent who hunted out Hungarian girls

Professionals working with such infrastructure are required to wear specially designed arc-rated personal protective equipment (PPE) that meets international standards.

The teenage boy died instantly at the scene, while the girl suffered severe burns over more than 70 per cent of her body and later died in hospital.

Another 16-year-old girl who was with them did not climb onto the train and was therefore unharmed. However, she was severely shocked by the incident and was taken to hospital after witnessing what had happened to her friends.

World.title: Yemeni Ambassador Ahmed Abdullah Nagi: Why the world should not allow Bab al-Mandab to become “another Hormuz”
World.content:
Bab al-Mandab Between Global Security and Human Tragedy in Yemen.

By: Ambassador Ahmed Abdullah Nagi

Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of the Republic of Yemen in Budapest

Bab al-Mandab is no longer merely a maritime passage connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden; it has become one of the most important indicators of stability in the global economic system. Every threat targeting this strait has direct repercussions on international trade, energy security, supply chains, shipping costs and insurance rates. With the escalating Houthi attacks on maritime navigation, the international community faces a real test: Will it act preemptively to prevent Bab al-Mandab from becoming another Hormuz, or will it merely manage crises after they occur?

Approximately 13% of global trade passes through Bab al-Mandab, along with significant part of the oil and gas exports destined for Europe and Asia. This means any sustained disruption in this passage threatens not only regional nations but the entire global economy through increased shipping and insurance costs, supply chain disruptions, and rising energy and commodity prices. Therefore, the security of Bab al-Mandab is no longer merely a Yemeni or Middle Eastern issue, it has become a shared international concern.

Ambassador Ahmed Abdullah Nagi

In this context, recent threats issued by Houthi militias claiming to impose an “embargo” on Saudi maritime navigation in the Red Sea are unjustified. These terrorist militias argue this blockade on the Saudi maritime navigation is a response to the blockade on Yemen. In reality, there is no blockade on Yemen; rather, there are restrictions on Houthi movement following their 2014 coup, specifically since 2015, under international decisions, most importantly UN Security Council Resolution 2216 of 2015.

In contrast, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has provided unlimited humanitarian, developmental, and economic support to the Yemeni people during the worst phase of Yemen’s contemporary history. Without this support, the suffering of the Yemeni people would have intensified and worsened.

Official data indicates the continued flow of commercial and relief ships to ports under Houthi control. Since the beginning of 2026, more than 300 ships have entered these ports, including 157 ships loaded with food supplies, 104 ships carrying construction materials, and 45 ships carrying petroleum derivatives. These figures weaken the narrative of a comprehensive blockade and confirm the continuation of trade movements and humanitarian supplies.

On the contrary, military developments indicate the growing offensive capabilities of the Houthis on Yemen’s western coast, including the deployment of missiles, drones, and attack boats, in addition to reports of continued Iranian logistical and intelligence support, including the return of the Iranian ship previously known as “Saviz” to the Red Sea under a new name. This reflects that what is occurring does not represent an isolated local development, but rather falls within a broader Iranian strategy seeking to possess leverage over the most important international maritime passages.

From here emerges the comparison with the Strait of Hormuz. The world has become accustomed over past decades to dealing with threats targeting that strait as part of the security landscape in the Gulf, despite the economic disruptions they cause. Today, the international community faces the possibility of repeating the same scenario in Bab al-Mandab, but through Iranian proxies in Yemen, as the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab experience escalating threats directed against international navigation, amid the continued use of this vital maritime passage by the Iranian-backed Houthi group as a political and military pressure card. If disrupting navigation or threatening with it become an acceptable political tool, the world will face a dangerous precedent threatening one of the most critical maritime passages of the twenty-first century. The danger lies not only in the direct impact on commercial ships but in the potential establishment of a new maritime security equation in the region based on using international passages as means to impose political will and achieve geopolitical gains.

Saudi Arabia: From Crisis Management to Peacemaking Opportunities

Amid these challenges, the pivotal role played by Saudi Arabia in supporting Yemen’s stability cannot be overlooked. Since the beginning of the crisis, the Saudi role has not been limited to supporting the legitimate Yemeni Government, but has included launching one of the largest humanitarian and development assistance programs through King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center, supporting the Central Bank of Yemen, financing the fuel needed to continue basic services, and implementing projects in the health, education, water and food security sectors. This support has mitigated humanitarian deterioration and prevented complete state institutional collapse.

Saudi Arabia also played a central role in promoting political solutions, leading—in coordination with Oman and the United Nations—intensive efforts to end the war and achieve comprehensive settlement. The Yemeni Government has shown clear flexibility in engaging with these initiatives, based on its conviction that the just peace is the only path to end Yemeni suffering and rebuild the state. However, continued military escalation by the Houthis has prevented tangible progress, highlighting the need for a more forceful international stance supporting the peace process and holding obstructing parties accountable.

Yemen: When Children Become the Greatest Victims

Maritime security cannot be separated from the humanitarian reality in Yemen. While the world focuses on ship movements in the Red Sea, millions of Yemenis suffer one of the worst humanitarian crises in modern times. War has destroyed the economy, weakened state institutions, caused essential services to decline, and pushed millions of families into poverty and displacement.

Most painfully, the primary victims of this war are the children. An entire generation has grown up in an environment dominated by fear and violence, lacking opportunities for education, healthcare, and psychological stability. These children need not only food and medicine but genuine opportunities to reclaim their lives and build their futures. If the war continues, Yemen will lose not only its present but its future as well, because state reconstruction begins with human reconstruction.

Therefore, supporting peace in Yemen should not be viewed merely as a moral obligation but as an investment in regional and international security. Each child returning to school is a step toward stability; each institution resuming operations reduces opportunities for extremism and violence; and each advance in the peace process directly reflects on Red Sea security and global trade stability.

Responsibility Beyond Protecting Maritime Passages

Protecting Bab al-Mandab cannot be achieved solely by deploying more naval vessels or strengthening military patrols, important as these are. It requires a comprehensive vision addressing the crisis’s root causes. Lasting stability begins with the Yemeni state recovering its institutions and sovereignty and supporting the legitimate Government, combined with promoting development and reconstruction efforts, in parallel with continued international pressure to ensure freedom of navigation and hold accountable those who threaten it.

Trump warns Iran over US troop deaths

Today, the international community stands before two clear choices: either taking preemptive action to prevent Bab al-Mandab from becoming “another Hormuz”, or waiting for a new reality to take hold in which global trade becomes hostage to regional crises.

Protecting Bab al-Mandab is not the responsibility of Yemen alone, but of the entire international community. It is the protection of global trade freedom, energy security, and international economic stability. At the same time, it is the protection of the future of millions of Yemenis who deserve to live in a safe and stable state, not on an open battlefield.

Yemen’s stability is the true guarantee for Red Sea security, and Red Sea security is an integral part of global security.

World.title: PM Péter Magyar launches probe concerning Orbán government’s EUR 1 billion North Macedonia loan
World.content:
Hungary’s government has launched an investigation into a €1 billion loan extended to North Macedonia, which the previous administration provided on preferential terms through the state-owned Eximbank, according to the North Macedonian news portal 360 Stepeni following an announcement by PM Péter Magyar.

Péter Magyar launched probe concerning North Macedonia loan

According to the report, the Hungarian government is reviewing four transactions linked to the state Eximbank, one of which concerns the loan granted to North Macedonia on favourable terms by the previous cabinet. The prime minister is said to believe that the conditions of the loan — a 3.25 per cent fixed interest rate and unrestricted use — were significantly more advantageous than those under which the Hungarian state itself can borrow, or those available to Hungarian businesses. As a result, suspicions have arisen that the previous government may have used financial instruments intended to support domestic enterprises for foreign political purposes.

The North Macedonian loan agreement was concluded in mid-July 2024 by Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski shortly after taking office, during a meeting with his then Hungarian counterpart Viktor Orbán on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Washington, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

If you missed: Hungarian lawyers’ circle head: former PM Orbán may soon become a suspect – can he be arrested?

North Macedonia subsequently entered into two €500 million agreements with Eximbank: the first was signed on 8 October, with a 15-year maturity, a three-year grace period and a fixed interest rate of 3.25 per cent. The second €500 million loan was signed in December 2024. According to 360 Stepeni, North Macedonia used part of the Hungarian loan to support businesses, with the remainder allocated to municipal investment projects.

Mr Magyar said the interest equalisation linked to the transaction, which is backed by a full state guarantee, imposes a burden of more than 90 billion forints on Hungary’s budget.

World.title: Breaking – Football superpower to arrive in Budapest: Real Madrid to face Ferencváros in August
World.content:
It has now been made official that the Groupama Arena will host a prestigious international pre-season fixture this summer, as Ferencváros welcome Real Madrid to Budapest on Saturday, 8 August. The encounter will form part of the Spanish giants’ Austrian training programme and is set to rank among the most high-profile summer matches seen in Hungary in recent decades. Ticket sales for the Budapest Real Madrid match will begin shortly.

Reports of the fixture had previously circulated in the press, now confirmed by Ferencváros, according to Nemzeti Sport. The record-breaking Spanish club is scheduled to play several international matches during its summer preparations, with Budapest included as one of the tour’s key stops.

Mourinho returns to the Real Madrid bench

Real Madrid’s summer preparations began in mid-July under the stewardship of José Mourinho, who has once again taken charge of the club. The side will play its first friendly at home against CD Leganés before travelling to Austria for a training camp, where it will face a number of international opponents. The Budapest fixture is expected to be one of the highlights of that programme.

First meeting in three decades

Ferencváros and Real Madrid last met in the group stage of the 1995–96 Champions League. At the Santiago Bernabéu, the Spanish side recorded a commanding 6–1 victory, while in Budapest the Hungarian champions secured a valuable 1–1 draw. Ferencváros’s goal was scored by Flórián Albert Jr, a moment that remains etched in the club’s European history.

The two sides have not met in either competitive or friendly fixtures since, making the upcoming clash a special occasion for supporters of both clubs.

Mourinho’s previous link to the Groupama Arena

Notably, the Groupama Arena’s opening match in 2014 featured José Mourinho’s Chelsea side as Ferencváros’s opponents. The Portuguese manager experienced the atmosphere of the Budapest stadium first-hand on that occasion, and reports suggest this prior connection may have played a role in Real Madrid selecting the Hungarian capital as one of its summer destinations.

Don’t Miss: F1 Events in Budapest

Ferencváros may seek league postponement

The timing of the friendly coincides with a major fixture in Hungary’s top flight: Ferencváros are due to face reigning champions ETO FC Győr away that weekend. The Budapest club is therefore expected to request a postponement of the NB I match in order to prepare for the gala encounter against Real Madrid with a full squad.

Ticket sales to begin shortly

According to Ferencváros, ticket sales will begin at 2 PM on 27 July. For the first 24 hours, only current season ticket holders will be eligible to purchase seats, after which sales may be opened to the general public, subject to availability.

The cheapest tickets will cost HUF 14,000, while the most expensive non-VIP tickets will be HUF 46,500 in sectors C4 and C5.

Demand is expected to be exceptional, as the 15-time Champions League winners rarely play in Hungary, making the Budapest fixture one of the standout events of the domestic football calendar this summer.

World.title: New details in the Hatvanpuszta zebra scandal: illegal keeping, escaped animals, and carcasses dumped in a pig pit
World.content:
László Gajdos, the minister responsible for animal welfare, has ordered a full investigation into the zebras kept at a farm between Bicske and Hatvanpuszta in western Hungary, he said on Facebook on Friday.

In the post, Gajdos said the relevant official documents reflected “total chaos” in the case, adding that “one thing is certain: there has been no responsible ownership there”. He said some of the zebras had arrived at the farm with inadequate documentation and that permits were applied for only later. The owners did not apply at all for a special licence for five of the animals, he added as per the Hungarian news agency.

Of the 17 zebras, only 10 had been registered, he said. He added that one of them, called Tihamér, had been kept illegally and that his existence only came to light after his death. He also said there had been no proper fence, and that three of the animals escaped and froze to death. Moreover, he said, the carcasses were disposed of illegally and thrown into a pit for pigs that had died of swine fever.

Screenshot from Gulyáságyú Média/YouTube

“This is not animal protection, but grave irresponsibility … we will not leave it at that,” Gajdos said. He also added that there are currently 17 adult zebras and three foals at the farm.

World.title: Romanian director Alina Șerban’s debut film “I Matter” to premiere at Venice Film Festival
World.content:
“I Matter” (“Eu contez”), the feature film debut of Romanian director Alina Șerban (in photo), will have its world premiere at the 83rd edition of the Venice International Film Festival, taking place from September 1-12.

Written and directed by Alina Șerban, one of the few Roma female directors in the world, “I Matter” is a co-production between Romania (microFILM), Germany (2Pilots Filmproduction), and Belgium (Frakas Productions, Lemming Film), exploring themes such as overcoming fear, hope, and self-acceptance, according to the press release.

Spoken in Romanian and Romani, the film tells the story of Rebeca, a young Roma woman who is about to leave the foster care center where she grew up.

“We very rarely see Roma characters who live complex human experiences beyond stereotypes. And stories about what it means to be a girl, Roma, and part of the child protection system are almost nonexistent. Through ‘I Matter’ I wanted to build a bridge toward a deeper understanding of these experiences and, above all, to tell a story about humanity. The fact that this film is beginning its journey in Venice means a great deal to me,” said Alina Șerban.

The film was developed over more than four years together with young people from the social protection system. During this period, Alina Șerban created several documentary short films and theater performances alongside them.

The film’s cast includes Denisa Farcaș, Sorin Mihai, Angelina Pavel, Vanessa Dancea, Raisa Mihai, Juno (Alexandru Stancu), Alina Berzunțeanu, and Natalia Călin. Alongside them, 16 children and young people residing in the Casa Iosif and Casa Sara foster centers, part of the Măgurele Christian Social Ensemble in Bucharest, also appear in the film.

The Venice International Film Festival / Mostra Internazionale d'Arte Cinematografica will take place from September 2-12, 2026. “I Matter” has been selected alongside seven other titles in the Spotlight section, dedicated to audience films characterized by innovation and creativity in the way they engage with viewers. The film is competing for the Audience Award offered by Armani Beauty and the Luigi de Laurentiis Award for Best Debut, awarded by an international jury.

Winner of the Best Actress award at the German Actors’ Association Awards for her role in Gipsy Queen (2019), Alina Șerban is a graduate of the prestigious Tisch School of the Arts (New York), Royal Academy of Dramatic Art – RADA (London), and UNATC. In 2024, she was decorated by the president of Romania with the Order of Cultural Merit, in the rank of Knight.

She is the first Roma film and theater director in Romania and, for more than a decade, has developed artistic projects dedicated to children and young people from disadvantaged backgrounds, as well as Roma communities.

World.title: Anti-corruption prosecutors detain three directors of state-owned Romanian defense companies
World.content:
Romania’s National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) officially announced on Friday, July 24, that it has detained three directors from companies within Romania's defense industry, all accused of taking bribes.

The three are Mihai Rafiu (general manager of Uzina Mecanică București), Tiberiu Alexandru Pîrvu (general manager of Uzina Mecanică Plopeni), and Liliana Sorescu (commercial director of Uzina Mecanică Plopeni).

Alongside the three, an administrator of several commercial companies was also detained, accused of giving bribes and complicity in giving bribes.

During searches, prosecutors found EUR 500,000 in cash at the home of Tiberiu Pârvu Alexandru. Authorities say Rafiu, for his part, allegedly received RON 48,000 from the businessman detained in this case, divided into 12 installments, according to the official DNA statement.

Tiberiu Pârvu Alexandru also allegedly received RON 25,900 from the same businessman "related to contracts concluded with the commercial companies effectively managed by defendant V.M."

The same businessman allegedly also bribed Liliana Sorescu. According to DNA, the total amount she allegedly received as bribes was RON 24,250, in several installments.

In addition, DNA also claimed that another businessman, who owns a company with contracts with Uzina Mecanică Plopeni, allegedly gave Liliana Sorescu USD 3,800, for "placing orders and carrying out the formalities necessary for the acceptance of the goods delivered by the respective companies."

Liliana Sorescu allegedly claimed that the dollars she received were counterfeit and requested the same amount once again, which she allegedly received in lei. "The contracts concluded by the two factories with the aforementioned commercial companies mainly concerned maintenance services, the purchase of materials, and the provision of services," DNA emphasized.

Reacting to the detention of the three directors, economy minister Irineu Darau said that "in general, the defense industry is an extremely sensitive subject. I am convinced that for some it is also a subject of temptation. A strong Romanian state must identify anyone connected to the defense industry who engages in dishonest activities.”

ROMARM, Romania's national state-owned defense company and the country's primary producer and exporter of military equipment, said in connection with the detention that it will support any legal action aimed at strengthening and reviving the defense industry.

The company noted that the problems within its subsidiaries have been known for some time and have been repeatedly brought to the attention of the Ministry of Economy, without answer.

The company's general manager, Răzvan Pîrcălăbescu, said in a statement cited by Digi24 that the reform plan was drafted by ROMARM's management, discussed with institutional partners, approved by the Board of Directors, and submitted to the Ministry of Economy for final approval, but so far the institution has made no decision.

World.title: Asia-born home improvement chain MR.DIY opens location at Bucharest’s Colosseum Mall
World.content:
MR.DIY, one of the world’s leading home improvement and lifestyle retailers, announced the opening of a location at Bucharest’s Colosseum Mall on Thursday, July 23.

Spanning over 800 sqm and developed following an investment of nearly half a million euros, the new MR.DIY store represents one of the most important openings within the retailer’s current national expansion plan, according to the press release.

The store offers a comprehensive one-stop-shop format offering customers access to thousands of practical everyday products across categories such as home improvement, household items, home organization, hardware and tools, stationery, toys, decorations, electrical accessories, car accessories and lifestyle products.

The opening is part of a process of diversification ongoing at the mall. Earlier this spring, Colosseum Mall also welcomed dm dogerie markt and Planeta Arthur bookstore.

The new store has been designed to deliver an accessible and efficient shopping experience, allowing customers to discover a broad assortment of products for everyday needs under one roof.

“This new store reflects our commitment to bringing the MR.DIY concept closer to Romanian consumers through accessible locations, a broad product assortment and affordable prices. Romania is an important market in MR.DIY’s European expansion strategy, and each new opening represents another step in building a strong long-term presence locally,” said Cătălin Secăreanu, representative of MR.DIY in Romania.

Established in Malaysia in 2005 with a single hardware store in Kuala Lumpur, MR.DIY has grown into one of Asia’s leading home improvement and lifestyle retailers, with a continuously expanding international presence across multiple markets. Today, MR.DIY operates in 15 countries worldwide, with more than 5,700 stores across Asia, Europe and other international markets.

World.title: EUR 80 million refinancing for Bucharest underground telecommunications network operator Netcity
World.content:
Meridiam and its partners have successfully closed the EUR 80 million refinancing of Netcity Telecom, the operator of Bucharest's underground telecommunications network, the company announced.

According to the company, the refinancing operation, led end-to-end by Meridiam, represents the first project finance bond issuance in the country, and establishes a new market record with tenors of up to 26.5 years, surpassing Meridiam's previous 18-year market benchmark achieved in 2022.

The operation also provides flexibility to support a future expansion of the Netcity Telecom network and new digital infrastructure developments across Bucharest, Meridiam said.

Netcity Telecom has been operating the underground telecommunications network in Bucharest since 2008, in a 49-year concession agreement with the Bucharest City Hall.

It has so far developed more than 3,000 kilometers of underground telecommunications infrastructure across Bucharest, while removing overhead cables. Today, the network serves around 70,000 buildings, representing approximately half of all buildings in the city, and provides internet access to nearly 600,000 homes and office premises.

Netcity Telecom has worked with several districts of Bucharest in designing and deploying dedicated fiber networks for municipal CCTV projects. The company has also contributed to the implementation of the pilot phase of the new Bucharest Traffic Management System, and is currently involved in Smart School initiatives.

Meridiam has an 80% stake in Netcity Telecom, alongside E-INFRA Group (20%), a Romanian group active in the energy, construction, and telecommunications sectors.

Meridiam, an independent investment Benefit Corporation and asset manager, was founded in 2005 by Thierry Déau. The firm specializes in the development, financing, and long-term management of public infrastructure across three sectors: sustainable mobility, critical public services, and innovative low-carbon solutions. With offices in Addis Ababa, Amman, Dakar, Istanbul, Johannesburg, Libreville, Luxembourg, Paris, Vienna, and Washington, Meridiam manages USD24 billion and more than 130 projects to date.

World.title: Romanian manufacturer TeraPlast inaugurates polyethylene pipe factory in Spain
World.content:
Romanian building materials manufacturer TeraPlast Group inaugurated its TeraPlast Iberia polyethylene pipe factory in Spain, strengthening its expansion into Western European markets. The facility, located near Bilbao, is expected to serve customers across Spain, France, and North Africa.

The factory, inaugurated on July 23, is located in Okondo, in Spain's Álava province, about 20 kilometers from Bilbao. It has an annual production capacity of 16,000 tonnes and employs 79 people.

The opening follows TeraPlast's acquisition of the facility and forms part of the group's international expansion strategy after earlier investments in the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria, and Croatia.

“Romanian industry can compete and thrive at European level, and we demonstrate it through actions, not idealistic speeches. Following our expansion into the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria and Croatia, our entry into the Spanish market marks another important step in our international growth strategy,” said Dorel Goia, chairman of the TeraPlast Board of Directors.

The company plans to invest EUR 4 million in the Spanish factory over the next three years to increase production by 60% and achieve an EBITDA margin of more than 10%.

“The expanded production capacity will serve the markets of Spain, France, and North Africa. This will enable us to reduce leverage while generating returns on our investment for the benefit of the group's shareholders," Goia added.

According to the company, the factory has an established customer base in Spain, France, and Germany and will serve as a regional hub for the group's operations in Western Europe.

TeraPlast Group is the largest polymer processor in Southeastern Europe and operates production facilities in Romania, the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria, Croatia, and Spain. Its parent company, TeraPlast SA, is listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange under the symbol TRP.

World.title: Otokar starts deliveries of Romanian-built Cobra II armored vehicles
World.content:
Turkish defense manufacturer Otokar has begun delivering Cobra II tactical armored vehicles manufactured locally to the Romanian Armed Forces, marking the start of serial production at its plant in Mediaș. More than 780 of the 1,059 vehicles ordered by Romania are scheduled to be built at the local facility over the next five years.

The company said the first Cobra II vehicles manufactured entirely in Mediaș left the factory this week. A total of 216 vehicles, including four different variants, are scheduled for delivery in 2026.

The vehicles are being produced at Automecanica Mediaș, which has become Otokar's first manufacturing facility in the European Union. According to the company, the factory carries out the entire production process rather than only final assembly, giving Romania the capability to manufacture 4x4 armored vehicles locally.

“Romanian-made Cobra II deliveries have just begun. The first Cobra II vehicles manufactured entirely in Mediaș left the factory gates yesterday heading to the Romanian Armed Forces,” said Yusuf Fettahlıoğlu, General Manager of Automecanica Mediaş.

The Mediaș plant covers around 140,000 square meters and has been equipped to manufacture the vehicles to the same production standards as Otokar's facilities in Türkiye.

“Beyond the production line, the investment brings Romania what matters over the long term: advanced production know-how, technology transfer and engineering capabilities. The Mediaș plant is becoming a regional land-systems hub, capable of supporting not only production for the Romanian armed forces but also future export opportunities linked to NATO and European Union defence programmes,” stated Yusuf Fettahlıoğlu.

The Cobra II is a modular 4x4 tactical armored vehicle introduced in 2013 and currently used by more than 20 military and security organizations across 13 countries, including NATO members. For Romania, Otokar is producing several variants, including personnel carrier, reconnaissance, remote weapon station, CBRN reconnaissance, and ambulance versions.

The project has also expanded employment at the Mediaș facility, where the workforce now exceeds 300 people and is expected to grow to nearly 400 as production ramps up.

World.title: Romania wins one gold, seven silver medals at first Central European Olympiad in AI
World.content:
The Romanian delegation to the first Central European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (CEOAI), held in Cluj-Napoca between July 14-19, won one gold medal and seven silver medals, according to the Ministry of Education.

The event represented a historic moment for the international AI community, bringing together more than 90 contestants from over 20 European countries, along with invited delegations from around the world.

During the competition, contestant had to design, train, and optimize their own artificial intelligence models, starting from completely new datasets and requirements. In the two competition days, students tackled problems in diverse fields, such as artificial intelligence model interpretability, optical character recognition (OCR), mathematical and physical modeling, computer vision, and the security of machine learning models through steganography techniques. The competition tested not only the participants' technical knowledge but also their creativity, analytical ability, and rapid adaptation to problems without standard solutions, according to G4Media.

Following the interest shown by high school students from across Europe, the competition, initially known as the Central European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (CEOAI), received a new name, becoming the European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (EUROAI).

Emil-Andrei Burloi, a student at the International Computer Science High School of Bucharest, ranked third in the overall competition standings, winning Romania's first gold medal in international AI competitions in 2026. Subsequently, following the decision of the Ministry of Education and Research for the Romanian delegation to participate as a guest delegation, the official ranking was adjusted in accordance with the competition regulations.

Silver medals went to Ciortea-Suciu Andrei from the "Silvania" National College, Zalău, Morariu Tudor from the International Computer Science High School of Bucharest, Ilie-Goga Radu from the "Tudor Vianu" National College of Computer Science Bucharest, Dobre Darius-Adrian from the "Matei Basarab" National College of Computer Science in Râmnicu Vâlcea, Apostol Mihnea-Petru from the same highschool, Nistor Iulian from the “Tiberiu Popoviciu" Computer Science High School in Cluj-Napoca, and Asandei Ștefan-Alexandru from the Iași National College.

The national team was coordinated by Miron Radu (Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași) and Ciprian Păduraru (University of Bucharest). The national team's qualification was achieved following the ROAI stages, organized in partnership with Genesis College and the "Tudor Vianu" National College of Computer Science, with the support of the Nitro Association, Babeș-Bolyai University, the University of Bucharest, and Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași.

Throughout the selection stages, hundreds of students from across the country solved original machine learning and deep learning problems, training their own models and demonstrating advanced skills in a field at the intersection of computer science, mathematics, and research.
