World.title: Trump tariff wall set to stay after Supreme Court blow: analysts
World.content:
Washington – Circumventing the US Supreme Court, President Donald Trump has found a way to resurrect his tariff wall in a fashion that analysts say could prove more durable to legal challenges.

Just this week, Trump slapped sweeping new tariffs on 60 trading partners and saw 25-percent duties take effect on Brazilian products. Both cases involved an authority that has previously been used to impose levies.

Trump separately tapped an untested justification for 50-percent tariffs on many Canadian goods.

The actions and threats “underscore the president’s continued affection for tariffs, and that they are not going away as long as he is in the White House,” Asia Society Policy Institute senior vice president Wendy Cutler told AFP.

Trump’s latest tariffs of 10 percent to 12.5 percent apply to goods from 60 economies starting Friday.

They came after probes over forced labor concerns, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Cutler said this has a lower likelihood of being overridden by courts, noting Trump’s top trade official Jamieson Greer had carefully navigated procedural requirements before imposing duties.

More concerning was Trump’s targeting of Canada using the untested Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the Atlantic Council’s Josh Lipsky told AFP.

The justification was Canada’s alleged discriminatory treatment of US exports, with duties effective after a month.

“That’s more tariff-as-punishment” and could signal that Washington intends to keep less conventional tools at its disposal, Lipsky said.

This is an “uncertainty generator,” added Scott Lincicome of the libertarian Cato Institute.

– Court’s reluctance –

Already, Trump’s newest tariffs face legal challenges from small businesses.

As courts have earlier allowed the use of Section 301 for imposing duties, arguments against Trump’s latest salvo would likely focus on official findings that justified action, Lincicome said.

“That’s just not something that courts typically want to weigh in on,” he added.

Still, some argue that Trump lacks such broad powers to impose sweeping tariffs.

Within months of returning to the presidency, Trump unleashed a barrage of tariffs on US trading partners.

He invoked emergency economic powers to impose a swath of these duties quickly, a move deemed illegal by the high court this February.

Trump’s sector-specific tariffs, imposed under different legal authorities on steel, automobiles and other goods, are unaffected.

Officials have since launched Section 301 investigations, including on forced labor, to reinstate duties.

Lincicome warns however that past investigations were more substantive. A probe into China during Trump’s first term took a year to result in duties.

This time, probes into 60 economies including major partners like the EU and India spanned just four months.

– Hard to undo –

US tariffs are tough to undo. Former president Joe Biden, the Democrat who succeeded Trump after his first term, kept his predecessor’s tariffs on China intact.

Even if a future leader wanted to reverse Trump’s duties, revenue considerations will complicate the situation, Lipsky predicts.

Many countries were likely hoping the worst of trade wars are behind them, he said, but some may now have doubts.

The Trump administration has struck 19 framework or reciprocal tariff deals. Yet, threats of further duties loom with Washington investigating 16 economies including China, the EU and Japan over excess industrial capacity.

“The administration has been careful not to exceed the tariff levels agreed to in bilateral agreements,” Cutler said. “But partners are concerned that this assurance may not hold.”

Chad Bown of the Peterson Institute for International Economics believes Trump is missing a chance to address bigger problems like China’s rare earth export curbs.

Trading partners have to “fight a two-front trade war –- dealing with Trump’s tariffs and China’s export restrictions –- instead of just being able to focus on China,” he said.

While countries have expressed disappointment, Cutler said, there are no signs of retaliation, “knowing full well they would risk further US tariff escalation.”

World.title: Trump says hasn’t decided on big Iran strikes, Tehran getting ‘serious’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had not decided on whether to launch major strikes on Iran yet, as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.

His comments came after reports that an increasingly frustrated Trump was meeting senior advisors to discuss launching a large-scale military operation against Iran.

“No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if had made a decision.

“Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”

Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left a ceasefire in tatters.

The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members.

“We’re locked and loaded and ready to go. But we’re talking to them, so I think while we’re talking, we’ll see what comes of it. I believe…They’re very serious. They should be,” Trump said.

The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial midterm elections in November.

Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated his stance that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.

– ‘Massive attack’ –

The New York Times reported earlier that Trump had met advisors on Friday, while the Axios news outlet quoted the US leader as saying on Thursday that he was considering a “massive attack” on Iran.

Trump separately doubled down on comments in an earlier social media post in which he said he believed that Russia and China were not arming Iran, despite reports that both countries were giving Tehran intelligence to target US forces.

“I mean, I will tell you that President Xi said he will not partake, and President Putin said the same thing. I think you know I trust them,” Trump told reporters. “I don’t think they’d want to have me disappointed.”

Earlier in a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump had warned Moscow and Beijing not to sell weapons to Iran.

“If they did, it would be very bad for them — Certainly not in their best interests,” he wrote.

Trump said Chinese president Xi Jinping had told him when they met in Beijing in May that he would not arm Iran under any circumstances, and that Russia’s Vladimir Putin had made a similar promise despite the war in Ukraine.

“He understands that I do not sell Weapons to Ukraine, but to NATO Countries. They pay full price, and how those Weapons are distributed, I have no idea,” Trump said.

Trump has frequently taken a more deferential tone towards Xi and Putin than he has towards Washington’s own allies, saying that they must be respected as the leaders of major world powers.

World.title: Canada inaugurates US border bridge after cancelling joint ceremony
World.content:
Windsor – Canada quietly inaugurated a border bridge with the United States on its own on Friday, after cancelling a joint ceremony following this week’s announcement of new US tariffs on several Canadian products.

“This bridge is a testament of what we can build when we work together,” Housing and Infrastructure Minister Gregor Robertson told a ceremony on the Canadian side of the bridge, which opens to traffic on Monday.

“Our relationship has been challenged over the last few years,” Ontario Premier Doug Ford said of US-Canada ties, but added: “Let’s keep working together.”

US President Donald Trump marked the occasion with a social media post and a combative tone.

“Canada disinvited the United States of America to the opening of the Gordie Howe Bridge, which is fine, considering they are paying substantial TARIFFS to the United States,” he said in a post on Truth Social.

He added: “We changed the terms of the Deal so the United States of America now gets 50% of the Profit.”

The 2.5-km (1.5-mile) bridge connects the US city of Detroit and and Canada’s Windsor, and is named after Canadian-born ice hockey great Gordie Howe, who played for US teams.

The CAN$6.4 billion ($4.5 billion) cost of its construction, begun in 2018, was fully financed by Canada.

Trump on Monday ordered a 50-percent duty on many Canadian goods to take effect in 30 days.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was looking at “all options” in response to the new levies, and that he and Trump had agreed to “intensify discussions” in upcoming weeks.

Carney then faced sharp criticism following Tuesday’s release of a proposed agreement on financial management of the bridge, deemed highly favorable to the US side.

The terms stipulate that Canada will make payments into a US economic development fund of the equivalent of 50 percent of net revenue generated by the bridge for a period of 15 years.

But on Thursday, Carney said revenue sharing would only apply to funds left over after Canada has first met its periodic debt service obligations for the building of the bridge, under terms of a 2012 deal that “remains in place.”

“This is a good deal,” Carney told reporters. “I should have been clearer.”

In February, Trump threatened to fully block the bridge, insisting the United States had been treated unfairly in its construction and that it should be “at least half” US-owned.

World.title: Iraq accelerates journey towards WTO membership
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has increased its attempts to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), with the new administration advancing a process that officials regard as part of a larger agenda of economic reform and diversification.

Iraq’s accession to the WTO would bring it into the rules-based global trading system, compelling the country to match its trade policies with international norms for market access, transparency, and regulation.

While membership does not ensure economic development, many observers regard it as a significant step toward building a more predictable climate for trade and investment.

Iraq’s WTO entrance is part of broader attempts to promote private sector growth, attract international investment, and boost non-oil economic activity. The process also requires considerable legal and institutional changes, such as modernizing trade laws and improving regulatory frameworks.

Last week, a team from Iraq’s Ministry of Trade traveled to Geneva to finalize technical documents with the WTO Accession Division and the International Trade Centre (ITC), marking another step forward in the country’s accession discussions.

Since 2020, the ITC has been supporting Iraq’s WTO accession process through a European Union-funded program.

Its work has focused on providing technical assistance to Iraqi institutions as they prepare for negotiations and implement the reforms required by the accession process.

Beyond the discussions, WTO admission is usually seen as a long-term reform goal.

The process promotes greater transparency, more predictable trade policies, and stronger institutions, while assisting countries in aligning domestic regulations with internationally recognized trade rules.

These measures might help Iraq diversify its economy, enhance its business environment, and integrate more effectively into regional and global value networks.

Their success, however, will be dependent on ongoing political commitment and execution after admission.

As negotiations continue, Iraq’s accession process remains both a trade negotiation and a larger exercise in economic modernization, with assistance from the WTO Secretariat, the ITC, the Ministry of Trade, and the European Union.

World.title: ICC members vote to dismiss embattled prosecutor Karim Khan
World.content:
United Nations – International Criminal Court member states voted Friday to dismiss prosecutor Karim Khan, diplomatic sources told AFP, following disputed allegations that he sexually assaulted a female member of his staff.

Khan, 56, was suspended last month by a key governing body of the ICC ahead of the secret ballot in which 82 of 125 members voted to remove him, a motion that required an absolute majority.

According to the sources, only 13 states voted for Khan to stay in his post during the closed-door session at the UN headquarters in New York. A further 15 members abstained, while some did not attend the vote.

In May 2025, Khan stepped back from his duties to fight the allegations made by one of his female colleagues after an inquiry was launched the previous year.

The alleged victim, a Malaysian lawyer who worked as Khan’s direct assistant, gave her account of what happened in an interview last week with CNN.

The woman, who asked to be identified by her first name Sarah, described “an escalation of attempts” that resulted in physical assault.

“There is no way for something to be consensual when you have such a power disparity,” she told CNN. “What I think many people don’t understand is that Mr Khan was not just my boss, he was everyone’s boss.”

Khan, who has been in the job since 2021, categorically denies the accusations.

Speaking before the vote, Paivi Kaukoranta, head of the assembly that oversees the ICC, described the case as a “complex and sensitive disciplinary matter.”

“I trust that I can count on your cooperation to ensure that the assembly can address the matter in a way that fully respects the privacy and rights of the persons involved, as well as the court as an institution,” she said.

– ‘Credibility’ –

In an open letter published this week on X, Khan’s attorneys called on ICC member states not to remove him, saying that no wrongdoing had been proven.

They also warned the vote could endanger the independence of future prosecutors, an apparent reference to Khan’s headline-grabbing cases.

In 2024, he successfully applied for arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant over the Gaza war.

The ICC, which is based in The Hague, also issued warrants for the arrest of several key leaders of Hamas, who have since been killed.

Khan was the target of US sanctions over the warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant, as were several ICC judges.

Gideon Saar, foreign minister of Israel, said on X that Khan’s removal was “long-delayed” and said the arrest warrants were “an attempt to deflect from the serious misconduct he feared would be revealed.”

“These warrants, issued against a country that is not even a member of the ICC, should never have been sought in the first place and should be revoked immediately,” he said.

Before the vote, Stephan Rapp, a former US ambassador specializing in war crimes, told AFP he believed the evidence was sufficient to remove Khan from office.

“If they don’t, that may be the end of the court,” he said.

“It’ll destroy its credibility and make itself even more vulnerable to these unfair attacks from the United States.”

Earlier this month, the Trump administration announced a campaign against the ICC, threatening more sanctions and accusing it of posing “an intolerable threat to US sovereignty.”

World.title: Ferrari boss cautious after Hamilton and Leclerc shine in Hungary
World.content:
Budapest – Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur was quick to talk down his team’s hopes after his drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were first and second in Friday’s practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

The Frenchman warned of tyre problems, lack of data acquisition and too many interruptions during a scrappy session. He predicted all Ferrari’s rivals would go faster over the weekend.

It was also clear that Vasseur was satisfied with a strong team performance led by an untouchable lap from Hamilton who is seeking to become the first driver in F1 history to take 10 poles at the same circuit.

“So far, so good,” admitted Vasseur. “But it is only Friday and it is a good start, but let’s see tomorrow when it can be a different story. Everyone will improve.”

He added that it had been difficult for Ferrari to gain understanding of their tyres’ performance because red flags, especially in the second free practice, prevented them doing a “proper long run stint”.

“It was a messy afternoon with FP2,” he said.

Seven-time champion Hamilton set the pace with a best lap in one minute and 18.729 seconds to beat Leclerc by 0.148 seconds, leaving world champion Lando Norris, last year’s winner, third for McLaren, but adrift by half a second.

Four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull was fourth and George Russell fifth for Mercedes, but championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who missed FP1 when Mercedes gave his car to test driver Fred Vesti, struggled to 13th.

Verstappen said his car still lacks dependability.

“It was a difficult day,” he said. “Difficult to find a good balance in the car. We need to make the car more consistent on a lap and make it work on the long runs as well. So, there’s still some work to do for tomorrow.”

Russell said he was adapting to changes in the surface.

“It was quite a strange day out there for everybody. Budapest is an amazing track to drive, but with half of the track resurfaced it was super bumpy,” the Briton said.

“And a lot of it is breaking up around the last couple of corners, which is making it quite strange to drive on.

“Our single lap didn’t look great, but the long run looked more competitive. We feared Ferrari potentially and it seemed to be the case – they looked very, very strong.”

Hamilton, who is 45 points behind Antonelli in the title race, said after last Sunday’s Belgian Grand Prix that he wanted to intensify Ferrari’s efforts and was still aiming to bid this year for his eighth world title.

Hamilton has a career record 104 poles and will hope on Saturday to repeat his last qualifying success, which came in Hungary in 2023, as he seeks a second win for Ferrari this year ahead of F1’s summer break.

Victory would be Hamilton’s ninth in Hungary, equalling his own Silverstone record for most by one driver at one track.

World.title: Trump says EU to pay ‘very big price’ for Google fine
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened to hit the European Union with tariffs and a formal trade investigation over Brussels’ latest antitrust penalty against Google.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said the bloc “will pay a very big price for this illegal and highly unethical conduct, which I have consistently warned them about.”

He said he would “immediately initiate a 301 Investigation” into what he called the EU’s practice of “ROBBING” American companies, and said he anticipated a “substantial TARIFF” on the bloc “at the earliest possible moment.”

“The United States of America is not a ‘PIGGYBANK’ for Europe, nor will we allow it to be,” he wrote.

Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act allows Washington to probe foreign practices it deems discriminatory and retaliate with tariffs.

Trump’s threat came a day after the White House announced sweeping new tariffs of 10 percent to 12.5 percent targeting 60 trading partners including the European Union.

The fresh duties took effect Friday after investigations, and relied on the same legal justification under Section 301 of the Trade Act.

Trump has been moving to rebuild his tariff wall — and his ability to impose duties on short notice — after the US Supreme Court struck down many of his levies in February.

– ‘Committed’ –

The European Commission on Thursday fined Google 890 million euros ($1 billion) for breaching the Digital Markets Act (DMA), the bloc’s landmark law policing the conduct of dominant online platforms.

It was the first penalty imposed on the company under the legislation.

The Commission issued two separate decisions: a 460-million-euro fine for favoring Google’s own shopping, hotel, transport and sports services in search results, and a 430-million-euro fine over restrictions that stopped app developers from steering users toward cheaper offers outside the Google Play store.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had already criticized the decision on Thursday, saying the EU’s enforcement action undermined “constructive dialogue” and posed a “real risk” to transatlantic trade stability.

Under the DMA, the Commission can fine Big Tech gatekeepers up to 10 percent of global annual turnover for breaches, and up to 20 percent for repeat offenses.

An EU official said Thursday’s penalties amounted to just 0.22 percent of Google’s turnover.

EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen insisted Europe would not back down from applying its laws, telling journalists: “We are very committed to our rules.”

EU officials have repeatedly insisted that their digital rulebook is not aimed at American firms, though Washington repeatedly rejects that claim.

US technology giants have cultivated closer ties with the White House since Trump’s return to office in January 2025, with several companies lobbying the president directly over European regulation.

The renewed tensions test the trade framework agreed between Washington and Brussels last year, which lowered US duties on European cars in exchange for concessions from the bloc.

Both sides struck the deal to avoid a painful trade war, and it cleared its final legal hurdles in the EU only recently.

World.title: NTA sacks 47 officials in rejig, to hire 4 GMs, 16 young professionals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, govt sources said Friday.

The crackdown follows the

paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the medical entrance test again on June 21 after the May 3 exam was cancelled. Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility has been fixed for failures in national entrance exams.

The first phase of

rebuilding its workforce includes four general manager appointments and 16 young professionals through UPSC's Pratibha Setu portal.

The recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting Saturday, education ministry sources said. The GMs - who will head different verticals - will be appointed on three-year contracts.

Sources said 47 personnel have been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged ro-les were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.





The assessment and psychometrics vertical head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment. The test-centre operations head will supervise NTA's network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, exam day operations and coordination with administrations.

The information security head will serve as chief information security officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock security operations centre and compliance with data protection, information technology and CERT-In requirements. The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital forensics capability and coordinate with CBI, Intelligence Bureau, ED, state police forces and cybercrime units under Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

The Pratibha Setu - Professional Resource and Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants - platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC exams but were not recommended in the final merit list.

Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts. The appointments will be for 24 mo-nths, and extendable to 36 mo-nths based on performance.

The changes seek to reduce NTA's dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.

Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.

The overhaul will accompany changes to exam delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET.

The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.

Govt is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information, and impose tougher penalties for security failures.

World.title: Gen Z outreach: PM Modi asks ministers to shore up presence on Insta
World.content:
PM Modi on video

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way you responded to my video post and gave constructive suggestions, thanks to everybody. Your love will continue and our bond will strengthen," the PM said, reports Dipak Dash.His remarks reflected satisfaction, with officials calling it a "successful connect" with Gen Z, who have been wooed by CJP and other opponents. Within minutes, Friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views.This came barely hours after PM urged his Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram, saying it will help them stay connected with the youth. He was interacting with them after the Cabinet meeting on Friday. Official sources said PM's choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked ministers how many of them were actively using social media platforms such as Instagram.He said the platform has been popular with large sections of youth and emphasised using the social networking site to connect with them.PM Modi has been using Instagram since 2014.His advice comes amid a growing sense that BJP, which successfully leveraged mass use of WhatsApp to steal a march over its rivals, runs the risk of ceding the advantage in reaching out to Gen Z, which is not as enamoured of the messaging platform and is more comfortable with the photo & short form video service.PM Modi, a tech enthusiast, has repeatedly urged his ministers to hold interactive sessions with youth on this platform. He has said govt as well as BJP should more active on social media. Chairing the council of ministers meeting in Jan 2023, he had stressed that social media had emerged as the main source of information for large sections of the youth and its growing allure needed to be harnessed.

World.title: Bill moots 10 years in prison, fine of Rs 10 crore for paper leaks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on examination malpractices and paper leak mafia, Cabinet on Friday approved a draft bill proposing up to 10 years in jail and a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore for those involved in such crimes.

The Cabinet chaired by PM Modi also approved statutory backing for fast-track courts for trials of such cases and to dispose of them "within three months".

The decision came barely hours after Modi, in a message on social media, vowed the strictest measures to prevent paper leaks, which have a devastating effect on the country's youth. PM has said that the proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 will be introduced in Parliament and efforts will be made for faster passage.

TOI has learned that the bill will ensure time-bound completion of investigation. A senior govt functionary said the 2024 law has "helped a lot" and several gangs have been busted and actions have been taken in the past two years. Govt aims to strengthen this and address any shortcomings to protect the interest of youth, he added.

People aware of the development said the jail term for individuals resorting to unfair means and offences under the proposed law would be at least five years as against the current provision of minimum three years' in prison.





The jail term could be up to 10 years. They added that fines for such offenders would also be increased, though they didn't specify the amount. At present, the fine is capped at Rs 10 lakh for individual offenders.

Officials said that in case of organised crimes by a person or group of people, including the examination authority or service provider, the jail term would be 10 years with Rs 10 crore fine. At present, the fine for such organised crime is Rs 1 crore.

The proposed law is also likely to bring coaching centres under its purview for any malpractices by them.

The existing law is aimed at curbing leaks, unfair means as well as organised malpractices in recruitment examinations like Union Public Service Commission, SSC, and entrance tests such as NEET, JEE, and CUET.

World.title: SC agrees to hear PIL against police excesses on Monday
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Friday agreed to hear Monday a PIL by an advocate for framing and scrupulous implementation of national guidelines ensuring "no police officer or security personnel shall carry out crowd control, public assembly management or arrests in plainclothes without displaying identity".

CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate who was highlighting the issues arising from the July 20 protest march and police action.

In his plea, Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions by Delhi Police during Monday's CJP's march to Parliament, and suspension and prosecution of all identified delinquent police officers.

He urged SC to ban ârolling, repetitive, or blanket prohibitory orders in any area without an objectively verified, proximate and recorded threat of grave public disorderâ.

He also said the court must direct authorities not to prosecute any person for political dissent, academic critique, peaceful protest or criticism of govt unless there is a âdirect, proximate, and imminent incitement to armed rebellion or secessionist violenceâ.





The PIL, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, sought a declaration that âany use of coercive force by unidentifiable or plainclothes personnel during public assemblies as arbitrary, illegal and a major service misconductâ.

Referring to the earlier petition and his reported remarks, the CJI said, âHe (petitioner) said he has filed a petition and sent a letter to SC. On inquiry, we found that neither the petition had been filed nor the letter had been sent. How can a court entertain a plea without a single paper before it?â the CJI asked.

World.title: Amid manhunt for J&K cop’s terrorist killers, detentions spike to 3.5k
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday as police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups.

A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack last Wednesday, in which Qureshi, who was on Amarnath Yatra duty at Lal Chowk in Anantnag, was killed. âDue process has been followed in all detentions,â he said.

DGP Nalin Prabhat convened a meeting for a comprehensive security review in Srinagar, with participating officers presenting their assessments of the prevailing security scenario across the Union territory.

âThe meeting focused on the current operational environment, threat perception and preparedness of field formations,â a police spokesperson said. âThe DGP directed the officers to intensify area domination and night domination, particularly in vulnerable urban areas.â

Home minister Amit Shah had a phone conversation with the slain head constableâs son after J&K leader of the opposition Sunil Sharma visited the family at their residence in Lalpora Beerwah of Budgam.





Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha, too, made a trip earlier and assured the bereaved family of the administrationâs support.

CM Omar Abdullah was critical of the detentions and Thursdayâs controlled explosions targeting the family homes of two wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. âI understand the policeâs anger. But there is a Supreme Court order that such summary action should not be taken,â he said.

Recalling his first stint as CM when J&K was a state, Omar said he knew âat the time that this problem (terrorism) cannot be resolved without the peopleâs supportâ.

He said the backlash against terrorist outfits after last yearâs attack on tourists in Pahalgam showed that ordinary people do not support them. âEven today, people are angry that a police head constable has been killed so brutally. But when the number of arrests rises from hundreds to 2,000 or 2,500, that public anger risks being redirected against us,â he said. âI hope we take our people along with us in this fight.â

Ex-CM and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti said detaining thousands and demolishing the family homes of two âallegedâ terrorists âamounts to collective punishment that has no place in a democracyâ. Peopleâs Conference chairperson Sajad Lone warned that the policeâs response to one of their own being killed by terrorists would âdo more harmâ.

World.title: Ladakh outfit welcomes end of Wangchuk's fast
World.content: Gelek Phunchok, convenor LAB, in a statement said âthe LAB welcomes Sonam Wangchukâs decision to end his fast, a step it had consistently requested in view of his deteriorating health.â

World.title: Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3
World.content:
JAMMU: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic on the third consecutive day.

The suspension of all major pilgrimages in the Union Territory â Amarnath, Vaishno Devi, Machhail Mata, Shiv Khori and Sarthal Mata Yatras â in place since July 19, continued for the sixth day.

Officials said the NH was blocked at Deohal bridge, Samroli and Jakhani in Udhampur district, and Banihal in Ramban district. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure.

Amid concerns of fresh landslides and shooting stones along the stretch, officials urged commuters not to travel on the road until it was declared safe for movement.

Kishtwar district magistrate, in an order issued Friday, barred all movement along the Kishtwar-Paddar-Gulabgarh axis from July 25-27 â in view of rain-triggered safety hazards along the stretch, such as slippery road conditions, landslips and persistent shooting stones â until further notice.





All ceremonial and customary religious rituals associated with the Machhail Mata Yatra shall be performed symbolically, the order stated, advising pilgrims and the public against venturing towards Gulabgarh or Machhail between July 25-27.

Rain-triggered flash floods struck Barkuanda area in Bupp, Udhampur, early Friday, affecting several households. There were no casualties. Damage assessment was underway, officials said.

World.title: Haryana’s air pollution action plan: Centre suggests strict enforcement and accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR, and emphasised the need for âaccelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcementâ to ensure substantial reduction in pollution before the onset of the winter season when stubble burning and meteorological conditions raise the levels of pollutants.

The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on Haryanaâs air pollution action plan and multiple steps, which are being taken, with particular focus on legacy waste, road dust, industrial pollution and strengthening the infrastructure to enable accelerated EV adoption.

Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and senior officials of the state govt attended the meeting.

"The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality,â said Yadav while emphasising the urgency of timely action.

On critical issue of stubble burning that increases level of air pollutants in Delhi-NCR during every winter, Yadav urged the state govt to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres.





He also emphasised the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. He suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats, and asked District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management.

âThe state authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers,â said a statement from the environment ministry on the review meeting.

It said, âThe minister also reviewed progress on construction and demolition waste management and requested that the establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of legacy waste should be undertaken on a war footing.â

Referring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and biomass burning, Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100% collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning.

On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles.

He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the âParivartanâ scheme.

âThe minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the âNo PUCC, No Fuelâ initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Yadav asked the authorities to identify traffic congestion hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest,â said the official statement.

Reviewing industrial pollution control measures, Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units.

World.title: Mirwaiz, MP Rashid, MP Ruhullah, Lone question mass arrests, demolitions after Anantnag attack
World.content:
There is growing anger and anxiety among the leadership of the regional parties, including Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, Member of Parliament (MP) Engineer Rashid and MP Aga Syed Ruhullah, over the mass arrests and demolitions of houses of families of terrorists in Kashmir in the backdrop of the Anantnag attack, which left a policeman dead two days ago.

Addressing the Friday (July 24, 2026) congregation at the historic Jama Masjid Srinagar, the Mirwaiz said the past two days saw in Kashmir “large-scale detentions, questioning and harassment of youth across Kashmir, with over 2000 young men being picked up on allegations of being “over-ground workers” or OGWs”.

“An act of violence by one cannot justify collective punishment for all. The killing should be investigated, and those responsible [in the Anantnag attack] should be dealt with according to law. But innocent youth and their families should not be scapegoats and made to suffer,” said the Mirwaiz.

He said the reports of home demolitions of suspected militants, rendering their families homeless, “is another extrajudicial and unjust measure”. “Such measures deepen resentment and are ultimately counterproductive,” said the Mirwaiz.

Meanwhile, the Mirwaiz welcomed the release on bail of Kashmiri human rights activist Khurram Parvez and journalist Irfan Mehraj.

On student protests in New Delhi, the Mirwaiz said, “Young people raising their genuine concerns should be heard and engaged with, not subjected to policing and force”.

He said reports of pellet injuries among protesters “were a painful reminder of the devastating consequences of pellet guns suffered by hundreds of Kashmiris over the decades. “It is sad to see students in Delhi facing it now. Use of force cannot resolve grievances or issues whether in Delhi or Kashmir; dialogue, accountability and engagement are the only way for resolutions ,” he added.

In New Delhi, amid the ongoing disruptions in the Parliament, MP Rashid, who heads the Awami Ittehad Party (AIP), strongly protested against mass detentions and the bulldozing of residential houses in the Kashmir Valley.

AIP spokesman said that as soon as the House assembled this morning, MP Rashid entered the well of the House and protested against mass detentions and the demolition of residential houses in Kashmir.

“We feel the pain of the family of the deceased policeman, who was killed in the Anantnag militant attack. Above all, he was one among us. But how can you justify the arrest of 2,500 people and the bulldozing of residential houses? Nobody in this country speaks about Kashmiris and the state oppression against them. You have tried to silence our voices through illogical arguments and the use of brutal force. You have created a martial law-like situation in J&K,”said MP Rashid said.

The MP, who is currently serving jail in the Tihar Jail over an alleged terror funding case, said: “The use of force against protesters in Delhi is equally condemnable. But why, in similar situations, are Kashmiris not even allowed to express their pain on social media? The incidents in Delhi have once again raised serious questions about whether New Delhi truly treats Kashmiris as its own people. While policemen were being ruthlessly thrashed on the streets of New Delhi, the response remained within the framework of law and order. In Kashmir, however, when an unidentified militant attacks a policeman, cases are registered against thousands of people and entire communities are subjected to suspicion and punishment.”

He also raised the killing of an auto driver, Arif Hussain, in Bhaderwah during an anti-militancy operation. “It is a cold-blooded killing by the police. Before talking to Sonam Wangchuk and offering him juice to break his fast, (Union Minister) Dr. Jitendra Singh must answer how Arif Hussain was killed in cold blood in Bhaderwah. He did not utter a single word against that killing,” said MP Rashid.

National Conference leader and Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah 2,500 young men picked up in 24 hours under a phrase, “detained for questioning”. “It appears in no statute and carries no safeguard. And in the night, two homes were blown up. One of them had been demolished last year, rebuilt, and lived in for barely a few months. The Supreme Court has held punitive demolition without due process unconstitutional,” said MP Ruhullah.

J&K Peoples Conference (JKPC) president and legislator Sajad Lone also expressed concern over the mass arrests. “The actions of the J&K police after yesterday’s dastardly attack will do more harm. You cannot summon and arrest thousands of people because their name is included in the OGW list. The list is decades old.

He said most of these people are old, well into their seventies. “There is a concept of reintegration in conflict situations. People who have taken to arms are eventually encouraged and facilitated to reintegrate with society. I don’t agree with the concept of mass arrests. It looks more like community punishment. Please have a relook. We live amongst people here and are subject to questions. And which law of our country justifies this community punishment? It is patently illegal,” said Mr. Lone.

World.title: Six cops injured as villagers clash with police in Chhattisgarh’s Surajpur coal mine protest
World.content:
At least half a dozen police personnel, including a Deputy Superintendent of Police, clashed with villagers in Chhattisgarh’s Surajpur district on Friday (July 24, 2026).

The police said that they were attacked by a mob when they had gone to arrest an accused in a pending criminal case. The villagers asserted that the police team was accompanying a survey team for land acquisition for mining, a claim contested by a senior police officer. “The situation escalated after the police attacked an elderly person.” according to the village Sarpanch.

The incident occurred in the morning in the Dharampur-Madannagar villages within the jurisdiction of Pratappur police station where the police team had gone to arrest some accused,

Surajpur Additional Superintendent of Police Yogesh Dewangan told reporters without adding the context or details of the case.

“We had anticipated that there could be resistance to the arrests and had reached the spot fully prepared. However, we did not expect the opposition to turn so violent. The villagers resisted the operation aggressively, leaving more than six police personnel injured,” he said.

The villagers hurled stones at the policemen and chased them with sticks, he added.

On a question referring to claims by villagers that the police deployment was linked to a survey of land for a proposed coal mining project in the area, S.P. Dewangan said there was no land survey team accompanying the force.

Babulal Poya, the Sarpanch of the village, said that a police team along with a survey team of the mining company arrived at the village around 3 a.m. and took away his elder son, Birendra. This sparked a protest by the villagers, which turned violent, he added.

“This morning the police team arrived and took away my son after asking him to accompany them to look for me. I wasn’t at home at that time as I go to my fields before the break of dawn. When I returned I learnt that Birendra had been taken away and the protests had started,” he said.

On how the whole episode was linked to mining, he said that the police were accompanied by the survey team who had come earlier too. “They had visited earlier this month too. The village has not given its NOC for mining, and this is a one-sided action by the government which is offering far less compensation than the market rates and is not even willing to discuss the issue,” he said, adding that the village, whose almost entire population comprises Gond tribals and the area is one of the tribal majority areas listed under the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

The Hindu made repeated attempts to reach Mr. Dewangan and the District SP Yogesh Patel, but they were unavailable for comment or an updated number of injured policemen even as there were reports of that number being higher than six.

World.title: Plea in Delhi HC challenges internet shutdown around Jantar Mantar protest site
World.content:
Legal services organisation Software Freedom Law Centre, India, on Friday (July 24, 2026) moved the Delhi High Court against the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of Central Delhi amid the ongoing CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar.

The counsel for the petitioner mentioned the plea for urgent hearing before a bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia, which agreed to list it on Friday (July 24). The plea, however, could not be listed during court hours due to certain defects.

Software Freedom Law Centre, India (SFLC.In), in its petition, sought quashing and setting aside of orders issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs on July 17, 20, 22 and 23 to shut down mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi.

The petition said temporary suspension of telecommunication services, including mobile internet services, was “one of the most extraordinary coercive powers conferred upon the Executive” as it interferes with the exercise of freedoms guaranteed under the Constitution.

Terming the suspension orders “illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional”, the petitioner said they neither disclose any public emergency nor provide the reasons to demonstrate why a blanket suspension of mobile internet services was necessary or proportionate to any alleged threat.

“The present challenge arises from the Impugned Orders issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs directing suspension of all mobile internet technologies within a radius of approximately 1.5 kilometres from Jantar Mantar, New Delhi,” the plea said.

“The repeated issuance of six separate suspension orders over a span of seven days further underscores the necessity of examining whether each exercise of statutory power was independently undertaken in accordance with Section 20(2)(b),” it added.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran’s military says attacked U.S. bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait
World.content:
Iran’s military said on Friday (July 24, 2026) it carried out drone strikes against several American military facilities and bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait in retaliation for the latest U.S. attacks against the Islamic republic.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said that they targeted a data centre in Bahrain belonging to Amazon, according to state media, though neither the U.S. tech giant nor Bahrain have commented on the claim.
